patients.summary: Woman with long-stable schizophrenia (outside psychiatry, haloperidol and benztropine) and thiazide-controlled hypertension who joins in 2022. Over four years she is diagnosed with spinal osteoporosis, severe right hip osteoarthritis, diffuse esophageal spasm, dermatomyositis and BPPV; after her last visit in August 2025 she has an antipsychotic dystonic crisis and then a ruptured right PComm aneurysm with SAH.

documents.title: New patient intake
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking for a new primary doctor; her previous PCP retired and the office closed over the summer. Has Medicare through disability plus MassHealth. Lives in Ludlow with her partner. Sees a psychiatrist at an outside clinic and wants to keep that arrangement. New patient slot booked 9/13. Release of records signed by e-form for the old practice's archive custodian. Asked her to bring every pill bottle including anything from psychiatry.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
56F here to establish. Old PCP retired; records requested.

HTN: on HCTZ 25 for roughly a decade, no side effects she notices, doesn't check at home. Schizophrenia: diagnosed in her mid-thirties, stable for about twenty years on haloperidol 5 mg daily with benztropine 1 mg, both from her outside psychiatrist, whom she sees every few months. Says she has not been hospitalized for it in many years and that the meds 'keep things quiet.' Acetaminophen now and then for achy joints. No other meds, no supplements.

PMH as above. PSH: none. Allergies: none to drugs.
FH: mother with osteoporosis, broke a hip at 78, also had breast cancer; father had HTN and a stroke at 82; sister has schizophrenia and has had breast cancer.
SH: lives with her partner in Ludlow. Part-time admin assistant, currently on medical leave. Quit cigarettes ~15 yrs ago, about 12 pack-years total. Drinks once or twice a month. Medicare (disability) + MassHealth.

ROS negative except as above.
Exam: well appearing, calm, good eye contact, linear thought. BP as charted. Heart RRR without murmur, lungs clear bilaterally, abdomen soft and nontender, no edema. No tremor or abnormal movements noted. Gait normal.
PHQ-2: 1.

A/P
1. HTN, controlled. Continue HCTZ 25. CMP today.
2. Schizophrenia, stable, managed by psychiatry. Metabolic monitoring on antipsychotic: A1c, lipids today. Will copy results to her psychiatrist if she wants (she does).
3. Bone health: postmenopausal, mother had a hip fracture, ex-smoker. Ordering baseline DXA.
4. HCM: Tdap given today. Hep C and HIV screening sent (once). Mammogram ordered; she thinks her last was last year. Colonoscopy per her was ~3 years ago and normal, will confirm from records. Flu and COVID boosters when available next month, nurse visit.
RTC 4-5 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Bernice, everything from Tuesday's blood work came back in range: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, and sugar (A1c). Cholesterol is fine for your risk level; the LDL is a touch above the lab's flag but nothing needs treating. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Urine was clean. I'll send a copy to your psychiatrist's office as we discussed. Still waiting to hear back on scheduling your bone density scan and mammogram.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
27 pages from the prior PCP's records custodian, scanned. Abstracted:
- Problem list: hypertension; schizophrenia (followed by psychiatry).
- Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Psych meds listed as haloperidol and benztropine 'per psychiatry.'
- Colonoscopy 2019: normal exam to the cecum, no polyps; recall 10 years.
- Pap with HPV 2020: negative for intraepithelial lesion, HPV negative.
- Mammogram 2021: BI-RADS 1.
- No DXA on file.
Flagged for PCP review.

documents.title: Fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fill history pulled for med rec: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg #90 monthly-ish fills through August; haloperidol 5 mg #30 and benztropine 1 mg #30 filled every month for the past year, prescriber outside psychiatry. Consistent with what she reported.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid; Pfizer bivalent COVID booster IM right deltoid. Lots and expirations in the immunization record. Observed 15 min, felt fine, left with VIS sheets.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison: none available. Breasts are scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcification in either breast.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Indication: postmenopausal, maternal hip fracture, former smoker. Technique: lumbar spine L1-L4 and left proximal femur. Lumbar spine L1-L4: T-score -2.5. Left femoral neck: T-score -0.9. Left total hip: T-score -0.7. No vertebra excluded.
reports.conclusion: Osteoporosis by WHO criteria at the lumbar spine. Hip bone density within normal range.

documents.title: Bone density result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bernice, your bone density scan shows thinning in the lower spine in the osteoporosis range; the hips look fine. This is very treatable. I'd like to go over options at your physical on the 7th. I've ordered a few blood tests to do a week ahead so we have them that day.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wellness visit plus bone density follow-up.

S: Has read up on osteoporosis since the scan and is worried; never broken a bone. Wants to start something to protect her bones. Separately, breast cancer is on her mind with both her mother and sister having had it, and she'd like whatever we choose not to add to that risk if possible. No hot flashes now. No history of blood clots. Mood steady, sleeping okay, still seeing psychiatry.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily; haloperidol 5 daily and benztropine 1 daily (psychiatry); acetaminophen prn.
NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted. Unremarkable exam: heart regular, no murmur; lungs clear; abdomen benign; spine nontender; no edema; skin clear. Gait steady. PHQ-9 = 2.
Labs 1/31: Ca 9.8, phos 3.5, alk phos 70, Cr 0.9, TSH 2.1. No secondary cause evident.
DXA 1/24: L1-L4 T -2.5; femoral neck -0.9, total hip -0.7.

A/P
1. Osteoporosis, lumbar spine, no fracture. Talked through bisphosphonates vs raloxifene. Given her family history of breast cancer and preference, starting raloxifene 60 mg daily. Reviewed clot risk and what leg swelling or chest symptoms would mean. Vitamin D3 1000 units daily; aim for about 1200 mg calcium a day mostly from food. Weight-bearing walking. Repeat DXA in two years.
2. HTN: at goal, continue HCTZ.
3. Schizophrenia: stable, per psychiatry.
4. HCM: mammogram 11/22 negative. Colonoscopy 2019 normal. Pap/HPV 2020 negative, next due 2025. Shingrix series to start, nurse visit next month.
Follow up in about 6 months.

documents.title: Prior authorization - raloxifene
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed a PA request for raloxifene 60 mg from the MassHealth plan. Completed with DXA T-score and diagnosis; submitted electronically. Approval came back same afternoon, valid 12 months. Pharmacy notified, pt called and told she can pick it up.

documents.title: Shingrix #1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1 of 2, 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Told her to expect a sore arm and maybe feeling run down for a day or two. Dose 2 due in 2-6 months; scheduled for mid-May. Tolerating raloxifene, no issues.

documents.title: Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second recombinant zoster dose, IM R deltoid. Says after the first one she was tired the next day and that was all. Series complete. She mentioned her right hip has been bothering her since the winter; suggested she book with the doctor to have it looked at.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - right hip
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
R hip pain since about February, slowly getting worse. Groin/front of hip, worst going up stairs or after she's been walking a while, settles when she sits. No fall or injury. No fevers. Acetaminophen takes the edge off. Pain 6/10 with activity today.
Exam: walks with a mild antalgic gait. R hip flexion limited at the end of range; internal rotation reproduces the groin pain. No tenderness laterally. Skin over hip normal. L hip full and painless. Distal pulses and sensation intact.
A/P: R hip pain, mechanical, likely intra-articular. She'd rather see orthopedics directly than do several rounds here, which is reasonable. Referral placed; they'll do films in their office. Continue acetaminophen up to 1 g three times a day max. Avoiding NSAIDs for now with the HCTZ.
BP up a little today, she's uncomfortable; recheck at next visit.

documents.title: Orthopedic consultation - right hip
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic surgery group. Date of visit: 08/07/2023.
Reason for referral: right hip pain.

Thank you for sending Ms. Marino. She describes half a year of right hip pain that has been creeping up, most bothersome on stairs or after a long walk, easing with rest. There was no trauma. She uses acetaminophen.
Meds per patient: HCTZ, haloperidol, benztropine, raloxifene, vitamin D, acetaminophen. NKDA.
BMI 32.
Exam: no redness or warmth about the right hip. Passive internal rotation is painful. Greater trochanter nontender.
Radiographs, AP pelvis and right hip, obtained today: narrowed joint space, subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.

Impression: severe osteoarthritis, right hip.
Plan: physical therapy referral placed with a therapy group near her home. Continue acetaminophen. Weight loss would help both symptoms and any future surgery. We discussed that total hip arthroplasty is the definitive option if she stops getting relief from conservative care; she is not interested at present. Return as needed.

documents.title: Hip follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called asking whether she needed a separate referral from us for PT. Explained the orthopedic office sent it directly; she has her first PT appt next week. Asked about taking more Tylenol. Reviewed max 3 g/day. She'll bring up the hip at her September visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up - HTN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine f/u.
HTN: taking HCTZ daily, no dizziness or cramps.
R hip: orthopedics saw her in August, films showed severe OA. Three PT sessions so far, doing the home program, thinks stairs are a little easier. Not interested in surgery yet.
Bones: on raloxifene + D since Feb, no leg swelling, no side effects.
Psych: stable, saw her psychiatrist last month.
Exam: BP and pulse as charted, at goal. Heart regular; lungs clear. No calf swelling or tenderness. R hip limited internal rotation, unchanged.
A/P: HTN controlled, BMP today. Severe R hip OA per ortho, continue PT and acetaminophen. Osteoporosis on raloxifene. Flu and updated COVID vaccines given in clinic. RTC early winter.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: BMP normal, potassium fine on the HCTZ. No changes. Message sent to patient.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 72. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. No ST or T wave abnormality. No prior for comparison.

orders.reason: intermittent dysphagia with non-cardiac chest pain

documents.title: Office Visit - dysphagia, chest pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: food sticking + chest pain.
HPI: Since around July, off and on, food feels like it hangs up mid-chest, solids and sometimes liquids. Separately, or sometimes with meals, gets a crampy pain behind the breastbone that doesn't travel anywhere and passes on its own. Tried Tums-type antacids with no help. Not brought on by exertion; walks to PT without it. No vomiting, no weight loss she's noticed, no black stools.
Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Comfortable. Chest wall nontender. Heart RRR, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.
ECG in office: sinus, normal intervals, no ST-T changes.
A/P: Intermittent dysphagia to solids and liquids with cramp-like retrosternal pain unrelated to effort and unaffected by antacids; normal ECG. Pattern sounds esophageal rather than cardiac. Referring to GI for evaluation (they'll likely want a swallow study and possibly manometry). Told her to go to the ED for chest pain that is prolonged, exertional or comes with shortness of breath or sweating.
Weight stable.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with 11/08/2022. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No new mass, distortion or suspicious calcifications. Stable appearance.

documents.title: Mammogram
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Your mammogram from yesterday was normal. Next one in a year.

conditions.label: Dyskinesia of esophagus
conditions.note: diffuse esophageal spasm pattern on esophagram and manometry

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology practice. Initial visit 01/29/2024; studies completed in February.

Dear colleague,
I saw Ms. Marino, 57, for half a year of on-and-off difficulty swallowing and chest pain your office judged non-cardiac. The pain is crampy, stays in the chest, sometimes comes with eating, and antacids have not helped. Your ECG from November was normal.
Current medicines: hydrochlorothiazide, haloperidol, benztropine, raloxifene, vitamin D, acetaminophen as needed. No drug allergies.
Examination was normal.

Barium esophagram: intermittent segments of simultaneous contraction producing a corkscrew configuration of the esophagus.
High-resolution esophageal manometry: multiple simultaneous contractions in the mid and distal esophagus.

Impression: esophageal dysmotility, diffuse esophageal spasm pattern.
Recommendations: small bites, eat slowly and sitting upright, drink fluids with meals, avoid very hot or cold drinks. Follow up here as needed if symptoms worsen.

Sincerely,
Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did you get the letter from the stomach doctor? They said my food pipe squeezes all at once instead of in a wave. They didn't give me a pill, just told me how to eat. Is that right?

documents.title: Re: GI letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, it came in yesterday. That's a fair summary: the muscle of your esophagus contracts in a spasm pattern. Eating slowly, small bites and sitting up are the first step. Let's talk about how it's going at your physical on the 19th.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent.
Interval: GI work-up done: esophagram with corkscrew segments, manometry with simultaneous contractions, called esophageal dysmotility with spasm pattern; diet measures only. She says eating slowly has helped some; still gets the crampy chest episodes now and then. R hip: finished PT, does the exercises most days, stairs still the hardest part. Raloxifene going fine. Psych stable.
Functional: independent at home, partner helps with heavy shopping because of the hip. No falls in the past year. Hearing and vision fine by report.
PHQ-9 3. AUDIT-C 1.
Meds reviewed, unchanged: HCTZ 25, haloperidol 5, benztropine 1, raloxifene 60, D3 1000, acetaminophen prn.
Exam: BP at goal. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft. R hip internal rotation painful and limited. No edema. Skin without rash.
A/P
- HTN: controlled.
- Esophageal dysmotility: continue GI's measures.
- Severe R hip OA: home program, acetaminophen. Ortho prn.
- Osteoporosis: raloxifene; DXA due early 2025.
- Schizophrenia: psychiatry; annual metabolic labs today with CBC/CMP/lipids/A1c.
- HCM: mammogram 11/23 negative, colonoscopy 2019 normal, Pap due next year.
Advance directive packet given; she wants to talk to her partner first.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC, CMP, lipids and A1c all within normal limits. Sent to patient via portal and copy faxed to psychiatry.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill requests: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and raloxifene 60 mg, 90-day supplies. Last BP visit within the year, labs current. Sent per protocol, 3 refills each. Raloxifene PA renewed through the plan portal last month.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - weakness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Since early May her arms and legs feel weak, close to the body: hard to get up from a low chair without pushing off, hard to hold her arms up to wash her hair, and the stairs are worse in a way that feels different from the hip. Not sore muscles so much as no power. No rash. No double vision, swallowing about the same as before, no numbness. No new medicines; no statin. Afebrile.
Exam: hip flexors and deltoids 4/5 both sides, distal strength full and symmetric. Reflexes 2+ and equal. Sensation intact. Skin: no rash on face, hands or chest. Neck flexion slightly weak.
A/P: Symmetric proximal weakness over ~10 weeks. Concern for an inflammatory myopathy; also checking thyroid and electrolytes. CK, ESR, TSH, BMP today. Will call with results and move rheumatology up if CK is high.

orders.reason: proximal weakness with CK 980 and ESR 40

documents.title: Results - CK
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. CK 980, ESR 40; TSH and BMP normal. Explained this points to inflammation of the muscles and that she needs rheumatology soon. Urgent referral sent with labs attached; I spoke with their triage nurse, who offered 8/6. Pt agreeable. Return precautions: trouble swallowing liquids, breathing difficulty or rapidly worsening weakness, go to the ED.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth daily
Take 6 tablets (15 mg) by mouth once a week

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology. Visit 08/06/2024.

Referred for proximal weakness and elevated CK. Ms. Marino reports three months of weakness in her shoulders and hips. About two weeks ago a rash came up over her knuckles and on her eyelids. No travel, no sick contacts, no new medications.
Meds: HCTZ 25, haloperidol 5, benztropine 1, raloxifene 60, vitamin D, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: red rash across the backs of the fingers over the knuckles; violaceous discoloration of both upper eyelids. Symmetric proximal muscle weakness of shoulder and hip girdles.

Labs: CK 980 and ESR 40 (your 7/16 draw). Here: aldolase 23.5 U/L (ref 1.0-7.5); ANA positive; anti-Jo-1 negative.

Assessment: dermatomyositis.
Plan:
1. Prednisone 60 mg daily, with a slow taper planned once CK and strength respond.
2. Methotrexate 15 mg once weekly with folic acid 1 mg daily. Baseline CBC and liver tests here; we will monitor every 8-12 weeks. Limit alcohol.
3. Age-appropriate cancer screening plus CT chest, abdomen and pelvis given the association of dermatomyositis with malignancy; ordered.
4. Sun protection for the rash.
5. Return in two months.
Given her osteoporosis, continuing vitamin D and her current bone agent is reasonable during the steroid course; defer to you.

documents.title: Chart update - rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rheum letter reviewed. Dermatomyositis diagnosed; prednisone 60 daily, MTX 15 weekly, folic acid started by rheumatology. Added to med list and problem list. CT CAP pending through them. She is on raloxifene + D for osteoporosis; continue. Will check in by portal.

documents.title: New medicines
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The rheumatologist put me on prednisone and methotrexate. Is it ok with my psych meds? My psychiatrist said to ask you too. Also I have a CT next week.

documents.title: Re: New medicines
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Bernice. There's no major interaction between those and your haloperidol or benztropine. Prednisone at a high dose can affect mood and sleep in some people, so tell me or your psychiatrist if you notice a change. Methotrexate is once a WEEK, same day each week, never daily. Keep the folic acid every day. Good luck with the CT.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (20 mg) by mouth daily; taper per rheumatology

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology follow-up, 10/08/2024.
Dermatomyositis, two months into treatment. Strength is coming back: she can rise from a chair without using her arms. Hand and eyelid rash fading. Tolerating methotrexate.
CK today 310 U/L.
CT chest, abdomen and pelvis (08/27/2024): no evidence of malignancy.
Plan: prednisone down to 20 mg daily, continuing the taper toward off over the next several months. Methotrexate 15 mg weekly and folic acid unchanged. Monitoring labs every 8-12 weeks. RTC 3 months.
Meds per our list: prednisone, methotrexate, folic acid, HCTZ, haloperidol, benztropine, raloxifene, vitamin D, acetaminophen.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP order: inactivated flu (trivalent) L deltoid, 2024-25 COVID R deltoid, PCV20 L deltoid lower site, since she is now on methotrexate and prednisone. Inactivated vaccines only. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction. She says she is on prednisone 20 now and feeling stronger.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with 11/28/2023 and 11/08/2022. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. No change.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - vertigo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Few weeks of short spells where the room spins, lasting under a minute, when she rolls over in bed or tips her head back to reach a cupboard. No hearing change, ringing or ear pressure. No headache, no weakness or numbness, no trouble speaking. Has not fallen.
Meds now: HCTZ, haloperidol, benztropine, raloxifene, D3, prednisone 20 (tapering per rheum), methotrexate weekly, folic acid, acetaminophen prn.
Exam: BP and HR as charted, no orthostatic drop. Cranial nerves intact, no spontaneous nystagmus, finger-nose normal, gait steady. Ears: TMs normal. Strength improved from summer, proximal 4+/5.
A/P: Brief positional vertigo, history sounds like BPPV. With her medication list and the recent myositis she'd like a neurologist to look, which is reasonable; referral placed. Meanwhile get up slowly, sit on the edge of the bed first. Fall precautions given her osteoporosis. ED for any vertigo with headache, weakness, speech or vision change.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology clinic. Seen 01/30/2025.

58-year-old woman with dermatomyositis and osteoporosis, referred for spells of spinning brought on by head position: tilting her head up, turning in bed. She has no hearing loss, ringing or sense of fullness in either ear.
BP 135/85. HR 78, regular.
Neurological examination normal apart from the Dix-Hallpike test, which brought on her vertigo with nystagmus that settled within 60 seconds. No carotid bruit. No JVD. No cardiac murmur.

Impression: benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
Canalith repositioning (Epley) performed in clinic and tolerated. Taught home repositioning exercises. No imaging needed. Follow up as needed if spells persist after several weeks of exercises.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology, specimen adequate, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit.
Since last year: dermatomyositis diagnosed by rheum in August, treated with prednisone and methotrexate. Finished the last prednisone at the start of this month per their taper; stays on MTX 15 weekly + folic acid. Strength nearly back, rash gone. Neurology in January called the spinning spells BPPV and did a repositioning maneuver; she's had maybe one brief spell since and does the exercises. Swallowing about the same, manageable. Hip same.
Psych: stable, sees psychiatry every 3 months, same meds.
No falls. PHQ-9 2.
Meds: HCTZ 25, haloperidol 5, benztropine 1, raloxifene 60, D3 1000, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1, acetaminophen prn. Prednisone off.
Exam: BP at goal. Eyelids and knuckles without rash. Heart regular, lungs clear. Proximal strength 5-/5. No edema. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected.
A/P
- Dermatomyositis, improving: per rheumatology. CBC and CMP today double as MTX monitoring; will fax to rheum.
- Osteoporosis: two years on raloxifene plus a 7-month steroid course. Repeat DXA ordered.
- BPPV: improved.
- HTN controlled. Esophageal dysmotility, severe R hip OA: stable.
- Schizophrenia: psychiatry; metabolic labs today.
- HCM: mammogram 12/24 negative; Pap/HPV today; colonoscopy 2019.

documents.title: Labs and Pap
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC, CMP (liver tests normal on MTX), lipids, A1c all normal. Pap negative, HPV negative. Results to patient; CBC/CMP faxed to rheumatology.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Comparison: 01/24/2023, same scanner. Lumbar spine L1-L4: T-score -2.5. Left femoral neck: T-score -0.9. Left total hip: T-score -0.7. No significant change from prior at any site.
reports.conclusion: Osteoporosis at the lumbar spine, stable. Hip density normal, stable.

documents.title: Bone density
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your bone scan is unchanged from two years ago, which is a good result, especially with the prednisone in between. Keep the raloxifene and vitamin D going.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill requests for HCTZ 25 mg and raloxifene 60 mg, 90 days each, approved per protocol. Raloxifene PA renewal resubmitted to MassHealth with the 3/25 DXA; approved.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up - HTN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP check, routine.
Taking HCTZ daily. No headaches, no lightheadedness. Rheum saw her in spring, dermatomyositis quiet on methotrexate. Vertigo hasn't come back. Psych unchanged.
She brought a flyer about a research study of a new blood pressure pill and asked whether she should sign up. We went over what a trial like that involves: she'd be assigned by chance to the new drug or a placebo, neither she nor the study doctors would know which, and the study would probably ask her to stop or adjust her HCTZ, with extra visits and BP checks. Her BP is well controlled on a cheap, familiar drug, which matters in weighing it. She's free to call the study team with questions; no decision needed from me. She took the flyer home to think it over.
Meds unchanged: HCTZ 25, haloperidol 5, benztropine 1, raloxifene 60, D3, methotrexate 15 weekly, folic acid, acetaminophen prn.
Exam: BP and HR as charted, at goal. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: HTN controlled, continue. CBC/CMP today (MTX monitoring too, copy to rheum). Annual visit due March. Flu/COVID in the fall.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts, kidney and liver tests are all normal. Copy faxed to rheumatology. No changes.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: HCTZ 25 and raloxifene 60, 90-day refills sent. Reminded pt by phone that her annual visit is due in March; she'll call to book. She says she had her flu shot at the pharmacy.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department, 01/28/2026. Abbreviated record.
59F, schizophrenia stable on haloperidol and benztropine, here with three weeks of her head pulling to one side and episodes of her eyes rolling up. Painless but upsetting and getting in the way of her day.
Meds per pt: haloperidol, benztropine, HCTZ, raloxifene, methotrexate weekly, folic acid, acetaminophen. NKDA.
Exam: sustained neck muscle contraction tilting the head to one side, chin turned toward the opposite shoulder. No fever, no signs of infection or injury.
CBC, CMP, TSH: within normal limits.
Impression: oculogyric crisis / acute dystonia due to antipsychotic.
Treatment: diphenhydramine 50 mg IV with improvement.
Disposition: discharged home with her partner. Contact psychiatrist within the next few days to review haloperidol. Follow up with PCP.

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I went to the emergency room last week because my neck kept twisting and my eyes were going up. They gave me something in the IV and it calmed down. They said it's from the haloperidol. I have a call in to my psychiatrist.

documents.title: Re: ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that, Bernice. I'm glad it settled. Yes, please keep after your psychiatrist this week, since the medicine question is theirs to sort out. If it comes back, go back to the ED. I'd like to see you too; the front desk will reach out to set up a visit.

documents.title: Scheduling attempt
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt to book PCP follow-up after ED visit. No answer, voicemail left with callback number. Portal message sent as well.

documents.title: Annual visit reminder
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Bernice, our records show you're due for your annual wellness visit. Please call or reply here to pick a time.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill requests for HCTZ 25 and raloxifene 60. Not seen since 8/2025; PCP approved 90 days each with a note that she needs a visit before further refills. Message left for pt.

documents.title: Emergency department and admission note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside hospital, ED and neuro ICU. Date of arrival: 07/25/2026. Abbreviated record sent at PCP request.
Brought in by ambulance after collapsing at home. Partner states she complained of the worst headache of her life moments before she lost consciousness. On arrival somnolent, rousable to voice.
History: schizophrenia, hypertension, dermatomyositis, osteoporosis, esophageal dysmotility, BPPV, oculogyric crisis on antipsychotic in January.
Home meds: HCTZ 25 mg, haloperidol 5 mg, benztropine 1 mg, acetaminophen 500 mg prn (per partner; list incomplete).
NKDA.
BP 160/95, HR 55.
Neuro: right pupil dilated and unreactive to light, right upper lid ptosis.
CT head without contrast: hyperdense blood in the basal cisterns, consistent with subarachnoid hemorrhage.
CT angiography head: aneurysm of the right posterior communicating artery.
Assessment: subarachnoid hemorrhage from ruptured right posterior communicating artery aneurysm.
Plan: neurosurgery consulted; admitted to the neuro ICU for securing of the aneurysm and monitoring.

documents.title: Call from partner
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's partner called (listed contact, verbal HIPAA authorization on file). Bernice collapsed at home Saturday night with a sudden severe headache; taken to the hospital and found to have bleeding around the brain from a ruptured aneurysm. Partner says the neurosurgeons sealed the aneurysm with coils on Sunday and she is still in the neuro ICU. Wanted us to know. Asked the hospital's HIM department by fax for her records. PCP notified.

documents.title: PCP note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Informed by partner of SAH from a ruptured R PComm aneurysm, coiled, in neuro ICU at an outside hospital. Records requested. Will reach out to the family once she is closer to discharge.
